analysis:
This PR touches only the CI threat-review tooling (.github/scripts/threat_review/*). It does not change the provider, coordinator, or native-runtime assets and trust boundaries in the canonical model (T-041 and others). I found no regression against those threats.

Changes examined:
- context.py: RISK/CRITICAL regexes move to the new depth_policy.py. The other helpers are unchanged. If any module outside this batch still imports them from context, the failure would be an ImportError, which fails closed. That is unverified and outside the supplied evidence.
- depth_policy.py: path_depth checks workflows first (Sol), then treats docs/, changelog.d/, test directories and *.md/.mdx/.rst as support (no path-based escalation). CRITICAL paths go to Sol, then delimited test/spec names go to none, then RISK goes to Opus. source_depth also uses previous_filename, so a rename out of a critical path still escalates. Sonnet findings or needs_deeper_review still escalate support files.
- budget_scan.py (head lines 339-411): depth passes are narrowed. The old rule that deepened the whole source set after integration findings is replaced by finding_batches, which targets the batches citing retained findings, and high findings go to Sol only for their own batches. Critical batches skip the Opus pass unless force_deep is set. Integration needs_deeper_review still records a manual-review reason. This reduces review depth and redundancy, but it keeps findings (all retained) and uncertainty flags, and Sol still gives a second view.
- plan_calls (lines 318-327): this is an optional budget hook, called only when paid.plan_calls exists. A BudgetStopped raised there is caught by run's generic handler and recorded. Its call-count semantics (bedrock_*) are unverified and sit in the unseen paid adapter.
- finished flag and diagnostics.py: the new keys are scalar and counter fields written to the content-free diagnostics artifact. I found no new secret or content exposure, assuming the bedrock_* metrics are numeric or enum values.

Residual observation: the support check now runs before the RISK check. Non-workflow executable files under .github/ in a directory named test/tests (e.g. a composite action) no longer get path-based Opus escalation. Only Sonnet plus its finding/uncertainty escalation covers them. This weakens CI-tooling review but is outside the provider threat model, so I did not report it.
